newsitem.title: USA: U.S. options exchanges want to shorten some trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. options exchanges want to shorten some trade.

text.p: U.S. options exchanges are hoping to trim trading in selected options by eight minutes a day to help limit market makers' risk, options industry sources said.

Four of the five options exchanges said they have filed applications with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) to end trading in equity options at 1602 EST/2102 GMT, and the fifth has not decided whether it will file.
Daily equity options trading sessions end at 1610 EST/2110 GMT, 10 minutes after primary markets close. Index options finish at 1615 EST/2115 GMT.

"Up until three o'clock Chicago time (2100 GMT), we're a derivatives market, but at three, we are not derived off of anything. We're a primary market," said an options trader at the Chicago Board Options Exchange.
"There have been cases where a company has released bad news at three and local traders and firms have taken it on the chin because there was nowhere else to offload" risk, he said.
"There's really no price discovery," he said. "Traders are flying blind."

Another options trader pointed out that stocks do trade after the 1600 EST/2100 GMT close of the New York Stock Exchange, but liquidity is low and bid/ask spreads are wide. "There is stock trading, but for all practical purposes, there is not," he said.

The CBOE, American Stock Exchange, Pacific Stock Exchange and the Philadelphia Stock Exchange have all applied for the earlier close. The New York Stock Exchange, which is planning to exit the options business, is reviewing the situation, a spokesman said.
The Philadelphia exchange's application covers only the close of equity options, not narrowly based index options.

Michael Schwartz, a managing director at Oppenheimer & Co and chairman of the industry group Committee on Options Proposals (CO-OP), said he was drafting a letter from the CO-OP to the SEC supporting up the exchanges' applications.

"We're in agreement of the exchanges going to 4:02 (1602 EST/2102 GMT), but only if it is implemented on a uniform basis," he said. "We believe that it is in the public's best interest that there be uniformity among options exchanges as to the beginning and ending of the trading session."
He said the CO-OP would appeal to the SEC to defer implementation of the earlier closes until all five exchanges submit applications so that closing times are uniform.
